accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:uniform-null-envelope-inference and thm:threshold-band-power-and-oracle-recovery
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The generic results assume that the DDD application supplies a regular cross-fitted reduced-form estimator, consistently estimated influence values, covariance convergence, and feasible envelope optimization.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform gain inference is claimed conditionally on a declared implementation satisfying the stated regular-estimation inputs; it does not assert that the imported DDD chart itself supplies them.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and paper Section 4 as cited in the proposal
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops DDD estimators with regression adjustment, inverse-probability weighting, and doubly robust methods and treats staggered designs with multiple comparison groups; it is an application input, not rank-collision inference.
The paper studies inference for known Hadamard directionally differentiable maps of regular estimators and gives derivative-aware resampling theory.
The numerical delta method gives pointwise inference for directionally differentiable maps and uniform validity for certain convex Lipschitz maps.
The paper gives generic conditions that turn drifting-sequence/subsequence analyses into asymptotic size and coverage conclusions for tests and confidence sets.
The paper develops second-order inference for functionals whose first derivative is degenerate, including locally valid procedures under an additional condition.
The paper studies tests of rank(Pi) less than or equal to r that remain valid when the true rank is below r, using nonstandard limits and bootstrap critical values.
The paper characterizes weakly regular parameters through underlying regular parameters and studies weakly efficient estimation.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Book metadata and contents; Chapters 2–8 cover basic asymptotic theory
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited book exists as the standard asymptotic-statistics reference supporting the fixed-dimensional triangular-array background.
The paper develops orthogonal-score and cross-fitting methods for valid inference with estimated nuisance functions.

The paper constructs singularity-robust AR and conditional-QLR tests with uniform size under weak identification and singular moment configurations; it is close prior art but does not target Delta(K,a).

Add Andrews (2019), Identification- and singularity-robust inference for moment condition models, and state precisely why its SR-AR/SR-CQLR construction does not test the nonclosed exact gain null or yield the proposed threshold-band result.

Add an application theorem verifying the regular factor chart and all procedure-side inputs for one explicit Ortiz–Villavicencio–Sant'Anna staggered-DDD score stack, including feasible semialgebraic-envelope computation.
Sharpen the OEQ into a concrete Gaussian admissibility class and a specified minimax or Pareto criterion, so the claimed power–diameter frontier has a unique decision target.
